audit.report: A merchant payout batch (protected_payout_batch, pid 778795) held an idle transaction for 4.1s, blocking one checkout session and degrading checkout success to 61% over 30s (~$7,156/min revenue at risk). The Database Guardian proposed waiting, citing the job's PROTECTED_SETTLEMENT class, never_interrupt policy, and non-replayable nature, with an estimated 36s remaining runtime fitting within the 60s business tolerance. The Continuity Guardian accepted after trade-off analysis showed waiting cost ~$4,281 vs. unacceptable settlement interruption risk. The blocker completed naturally after 8s; checkout recovered to 100% success within 10s and no protected settlements were aborted.
audit.root_cause: A protected settlement worker (merchant_payout) held an idle-in-transaction lock for ~12s total, blocking checkout sessions and breaching the 95% SLO.
lessons: For protected_payout_batch (merchant_payout): add a pre-flight lock timeout or statement timeout to prevent idle-in-transaction stalls from blocking checkout.
For protected_payout_batch: instrument the settlement worker to emit progress heartbeats so remaining runtime can be measured, not estimated, during incidents.
audit.negotiation_critique: The Database Guardian correctly prioritized data integrity by invoking the never_interrupt policy and quantifying the wait/revenue trade-off; the Continuity Guardian accepted without objection, making this a clean, single-round agreement with no wasted rounds or missed evidence.
follow_ups: Add pg_stat_activity monitoring alert for idle-in-transaction >10s on settlement_worker roles.
Review protected_payout_batch code path for the SELECT 1 idle pattern and add explicit transaction boundaries.
Run a chaos test simulating this lock contention to validate the 60s degradation tolerance and circuit-breaker behavior.

events.title: R1 proposes wait

proposal.rationale: The root blocker (pid 778795, settlement_worker/protected_payout_batch) has held its transaction open for only 4.1s and its last statement was a trivial SELECT 1, suggesting it is near completion. Checkout is degraded (82% success vs 95% SLO, $3,286/min at risk per BIZ-1) but the business tolerates up to 60s of degradation. Terminating a protected settlement worker risks data inconsistency and financial loss; we lack registry, calendar, settlements, and trade-off data to justify that risk. Waiting a short, bounded interval is the lowest-blast-radius choice while we gather the missing evidence.
proposal.expected_effect: If the blocker commits/rolls back within the next ~10-20s, its locks release and the 12 waiting sessions (including checkout) proceed. Checkout success rate should recover toward SLO without any forced termination.
proposal.risk_assessment: If the blocker stalls beyond the 60s tolerance, checkout remains degraded and revenue loss continues. We mitigate by requesting probes now so we can escalate or terminate with evidence if waiting proves ineffective.
